title: SDK Field Guide: resilient streaming, CLI-first workflows, and microserver blueprints
creator: Ayesha Kapoor
description: Create a pragmatic, deployable set of SDK examples and small reference apps demonstrating best-practice patterns for streaming ergonomics, retry semantics, and CLI-first developer flows across Python, TypeScript, and Go. Deliverables include: a Next.js edge-adapter example that streams tokens to a browser client with backpressure support; a FastAPI server example that exposes both sync and streaming generator endpoints with background KV-cache hints; a small Go HTTP server demonstrating efficient connection reuse, graceful shutdown, and channel-driven streaming; and a CLI tool (polyglot examples) that consumes streaming responses and supports idempotent retries and resumable streams. Emphasize observable behaviours (retry logs, token accounting) and testable contracts so product/DS can reproduce latency/cost comparisons.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Next.js example (typescript) that demonstrates streaming to client via ReadableStream and handles client disconnects gracefully; repo sample runs with 'npm run dev'
A2: FastAPI example (python) exposing /generate and /stream endpoints; includes sample prompt sets and CI that validates streaming integrity and token counts
A3: Go HTTP server example with graceful shutdown, connection reuse, and a streaming handler that forwards model token chunks using channels; buildable with 'go build'
A4: CLI examples in each language that show retryable commands with idempotency keys and exponential backoff with jitter; failure modes and resumed streams are documented
A5: Automated tests (unit + integration smoke) that assert retry behaviour, idempotency key handling, and that partial-response fallback occurs on timeouts
A6: Documentation (README + short field guide) describing trade-offs (client vs server buffering, batching effects on latency/cost) and recommended settings for production workloads
A7: PR reviewed and merged; design sign-off by SDK PM and Design lead; demo recorded for internal docs
comments: 2025-02-12 - Ayesha Kapoor: Kickoff spike complete. Prototyped ReadableStream approach in TS and AsyncGenerator in Python. Observed that per-request batching policies interact badly with aggressive client-side buffering.

2025-02-18 - Marco Silva: Decided to adopt an 'async iterator / stream consumer' pattern as the canonical streaming API across languages to simplify porting. This influenced the Next.js sample to use a tiny edge adapter that surfaces an async stream to the browser as a ReadableStream.

2025-02-22 - Design review (Tomas Nguyen): Prefer showing two UX patterns: 'progressive render' for conversational UIs and 'chunked batch' for high-throughput ingestion. Tomas asked for a small visual in the README showing latency vs cost trade-offs.

2025-02-25 - PM feedback (Elena Martinez): Ensure CLI examples include idempotency key usage and an explicit explanation of when to use 'resume' vs 'restart' semantics. Also requested a short table showing how retries affect token billing.

2025-02-27 - Engineering note (Marco Silva): Implemented retry shim for Python SDK using a decorator that attaches an idempotency-key header. For TypeScript we added an AbortSignal-aware retry wrapper so backpressure can cancel retries cleanly.

2025-03-01 - QA (Sofia Liu): Added integration smoke tests for the FastAPI stream endpoint. Found a bug where client disconnects were leaving goroutines hung in the Go server—fixed by adding context cancellation propagation.

2025-03-02 - PR ready (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples/pull/142 - contains Next.js / FastAPI / Go / CLI examples. Need one more review pass for docs and token accounting tests.
2025-03-03 - Marco Silva: Marking In Progress -> preparing final PR changes. Remaining work: add architecture diagram, finalize README checklist, record 5-min demo video for internal handbook.

Review notes (2025-03-03): Keep streaming examples intentionally minimal; link to full SDK patterns in the main docs rather than duplicating. Consider adding a 'common gotchas' section with example cURL commands.
